source: KICD Agriculture, First Published 2017; Revised 2024 (text layer)
status: outcomes from KICD's text, word for word; skills, prerequisites and misconceptions not yet mapped

learning_experiences: watch video clips or observe photographs or make field excursions to observe types of soil erosion,
demonstrate how to control various types of soil erosion (gulley, rill, splash and sheet erosion),
discuss and make class presentations to appreciate the importance of controlling soil erosion to conserve soil in their environment.
key_inquiry_questions: How does erosion control conserve the environment?
sub_strands.core_competences: Critical thinking and problem solving: evaluation and decision making skills as learners explore appropriate ways of controlling soil erosion.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: proactively solving problems by taking appropriate measures to control soil erosion.
sub_strands.pcis: Environmental awareness as learners undertake control of soil erosion in the school environment.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate control of soil erosion to knowledge on conservation of natural resources learnt in Social Studies.

outcomes.text: describe types of soil erosion in the environment
control soil erosion in the environment
appreciate importance of conserving soil

learning_experiences: watch video clips or observe photographs or visit sites to observe sunken bed and shallow pits,
prepare seedbeds that conserve moisture (sunken seedbed and shallow pit),
utilise the sunken seedbed and shallow pits to appreciate the importance of soil moisture conservation in crop production.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we prepare a seedbed to conserve moisture?
sub_strands.core_competences: Critical thinking and problem solving: open mindedness and creativity as learners look for possibilities for conserving soil moisture.
sub_strands.values: Social justice: fairness and justice as learners share tasks and responsibilities in preparation of seedbeds.
sub_strands.pcis: Conservation of resources as learners conserve water through preparation of water conserving seedbeds.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate conservation of soil moisture to farming activities learnt in Social Studies.

outcomes.text: identify types of seedbeds that conserve soil moisture
prepare different types of seedbeds that conserve soil moisture
appreciate importance of conserving moisture in a seedbed to increase chances of plants growth

learning_experiences: search for information on physical deterrents search such as mesh fences, thorny fences, safe traps, innovative lights, innovative sounds, and deflectors,
select and establish a deterrent applicable in their local context,
discuss with a resource person the use of physical deterrents to acknowledge the importance of conserving wild animals in safeguarding crops and domestic animals.
key_inquiry_questions: How can wild animals be kept away from crops and domestic animals?
sub_strands.core_competences: Creativity and imagination: exploration skills as learners seek new ideas to establish physical deterrents against wild animals that destroy crops and domestic animals.
sub_strands.values: Patriotism: consciousness of social and moral duties to conserve wild animals and promote biodiversity.
sub_strands.pcis: Protection of biodiversity against extinction by deterring them without killing them.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate conservation of wild animals through use of deterrents to knowledge on importance of wildlife learnt in Social Studies.

outcomes.text: identify deterrents that can keep off wild animals from crop and domestic animals
establish deterrents to keep off wild animals from destroying crops and domestic animals
acknowledge the importance of deterrents in conserving wild animals

learning_experiences: share experiences on routine practices in rearing of small domestic animals,
rear small domestic animal such as rabbits or guinea pigs to practise routine practices such as housing, feeding, watering, sanitation and parasite control.
make presentations to advocate the rearing of small domestic animals that are used for food.
key_inquiry_questions: How does rearing of animals contribute to food production?
sub_strands.core_competences: Self-efficacy: self-realization and confidence as learners rear small domestic animals such as rabbits for food production.
sub_strands.values: Integrity: fairness in allocation of resources and tasks in the project for rearing small domestic animals.
sub_strands.pcis: Animal welfare in the handling and caring for small domestic animals.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate rearing of small domestic animals to knowledge of farming as a socio-economic activity learnt in Social Studies.

outcomes.text: explain routine practices in rearing of small domestic animals
rear small domestic animals used as sources of food
embrace the rearing of small domestic animals used as sources of food

learning_experiences: watch video clips or listen to resource person and share experiences on how to preserve fruits and vegetables using sun-drying method,
preserve fruits or vegetables using sun-drying method,
utilize sun-drying method in preservation of fruits and vegetables at home to reduce food wastage.
key_inquiry_questions: How does preservation of fruits and vegetables enhance food security?
sub_strands.core_competences: Critical thinking and problem solving: evaluation and decision making skills as learners explore ways of preserving fruits and vegetables to prevent spoilage.
sub_strands.values: Integrity: choosing to do the right thing and being honest by observing ethical, hygienic and safe methods of preserving fruits and vegetables.
sub_strands.pcis: Food and nutrition security as learners preserve fruits and vegetables to avoid spoilage.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate the preserved parts of fruits and vegetables to the parts of plant learnt in Science and Technology.

outcomes.text: describe how to preserve crop produce at home
preserve crop produce using drying method
adopt preservation crop produce to reduce food wastage

learning_experiences: watch video clips or observe demonstration on stewing and baking as methods of cooking,
cook foods using stewing and baking methods (rubbing-in method),
serve foods prepares using stewing and baking methods.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we cook foods by baking?
How can we cook foods by stewing?
sub_strands.core_competences: Learning to learn: reflection of own learning to apply stewing and baking of foods.
sub_strands.values: Integrity: prudent use of resources and application of laid down procedure in stewing and baking foods.
sub_strands.pcis: Safety of self and others while cooking food.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate measuring of ingredients for baking to measurement of weights learnt in Mathematics.

outcomes.text: describe different methods of cooking
cook food using, different methods
embrace different methods of cooking in food production

learning_experiences: discuss and share experiences on practices that enhance body cleanliness (managing sweat, acnes and pimples, menstrual hygiene and care of pubic parts) for personal hygiene,
embrace applicable good routines that suit their body cleanliness,
discuss the importance of body cleanliness as a hygienic habit.
key_inquiry_questions: How does body cleanliness enhance personal hygiene?
sub_strands.core_competences: Self-efficacy: self-confidence skills while learners maintain personal cleanliness as a healthy habit.
sub_strands.values: Peace: tolerance for others while learners appreciate their personal and preferential differences relating to body cleanliness.
sub_strands.pcis: Personal hygiene as learners adopt body cleanliness practices.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate body cleanliness as a healthy habit to knowledge of growth and development learnt in Science and Technology.

outcomes.text: describe practices that enhance body cleanliness
practice body cleanliness as a healthy habit
recognise importance of body cleanliness as a hygienic practice

learning_experiences: use digital resources and sample articles to identify common stains (blood and grass) on clothing and household articles,
carry out removal of common stains (blood and grass) on clothing and household articles,
practise and adopt stain removal for personal hygiene.
key_inquiry_questions: How does stain removal enhance personal hygiene?
sub_strands.core_competences: Learning to learn: researching skills as learners identify and use different ways of removing stains.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: proactive engagement skills by removing stains to maintain cleanliness.
sub_strands.pcis: Personal hygiene as learners maintain cleanliness by removing stains from their clothes.
sub_strands.links: Learners relates removal of stains on cloths to knowledge of solvents learnt in Science and Technology.

outcomes.text: identify common stains on clothing and household articles
remove common stains from clothing and household articles
adopt stain removal for personal hygiene

learning_experiences: observe a demonstration by resource person, photographs, or watch video clip to identify crocheting stitches (single and double crochet stitches) in making household article,
use (single or double crochet stitches) to make articles such as mats, cleaning rug, and surface wipers,
construct articles using crocheting stitches and showcase the household articles to promote adoption in their daily routines.
key_inquiry_questions: How can crocheting reduce the cost of purchasing household articles?
sub_strands.core_competences: Creativity and imagination: originality skills as learners make household articles using crocheting stitches.
sub_strands.values: Integrity: prudent use of resources as the learners make household articles using crocheting stitches.
sub_strands.pcis: Financial literacy as learners save costs by constructing useable household articles using crocheting skills.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate construction of household articles made through crocheting to artistic skills learnt in Creative Arts.

outcomes.text: identify crocheting stitches in making household articles
use crocheting stitches to make a household articles
adopt the use of crocheting stiches in making household articles

learning_experiences: search and share information on the meaning of moist bed garden,
construct a moist bed (sunken or raised moist bed) using locally available materials,
establish and grow a crop of their choice to embrace the use of moist bed garden.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we construct a moist bed gardens to grow crops?
sub_strands.core_competences: Communication and collaboration: team work as learners share information on moist bed garden.
sub_strands.values: Respect: appreciation of diverse opinion as learners share information on moist bed garden.
sub_strands.pcis: Environmental conservation as learners use locally available materials to construct moist bed garden.
sub_strands.links: Learners relate skills used in construction of moist bed garden to craft skills learnt in Creative Arts.

outcomes.text: explain the meaning of moist bed garden
construct a moist bed garden for growing a selected crop
embrace the use of moist bed garden in growing crops
